_meta.purpose: Calibration gold-set for the §G analogue what_happened_next curation pipeline. Measures (a) generation accuracy vs ground truth, (b) adversarial-verifier catch-rate on planted errors, (c) false-positive rate on genuine-correct blurbs, (d) confidence-gate behavior on thin-source events.
_meta.ground_truth_authority: Opus (orchestrator) priors; the LIVE WEB is the real arbiter — verifiers must confirm against resolvable sources. Planted errors are FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION (a verifiable fact is flipped), so catch-rate is objective regardless of prior accuracy.

scoring.catch_rate: fraction of planted_errors the verifier panel marks FAIL/REVISE (target ~1.0)
scoring.false_positive_rate: fraction of genuine-correct blurbs the panel wrongly marks FAIL (target ~0)
scoring.generation_accuracy: fraction of pipeline drafts whose facts match ground_truth (target high)
scoring.confidence_gate: thin-source events should ship NULL (low confidence), not a guess

events.ground_truth: On 11 Sep 1973 a military coup led by Gen. Augusto Pinochet overthrew the elected socialist president Salvador Allende, who died in La Moneda. A military junta took power, beginning a 17-year dictatorship (to 1990).
In Nov 1979 Iranian students seized the US embassy in Tehran (444-day hostage crisis). The US broke diplomatic relations with Iran (Apr 1980) and imposed sanctions; ties remain severed.
Finland joined the European Union on 1 Jan 1995 (with Austria and Sweden), following a 1994 accession referendum. It later adopted the euro in 1999.
In Jul 1969 PM Indira Gandhi nationalised India's 14 largest private commercial banks by ordinance, a landmark state-expansion of the financial sector.

In Mar 2012 a coup led by Capt. Amadou Sanogo ousted President Touré weeks before scheduled elections. The power vacuum accelerated the Tuareg (MNLA) + Islamist takeover of northern Mali, prompting the 2013 French intervention.

In 2012 Greece enacted its second bailout with deep austerity and the PSI private-creditor debt restructuring (the largest sovereign-debt restructuring in history, Mar 2012). Greece stayed in the eurozone.

The 2008 farm conflict over Resolution 125 (sliding-scale grain export taxes) triggered months of lockouts. In Jul 2008 the Senate tied and VP Julio Cobos cast the deciding vote AGAINST the measure, defeating it.

Amid hyperinflation, the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe launched 'Operation Sunrise' (Aug 2006), redenominating the dollar by removing three zeros. Inflation kept accelerating, leading to further redenominations (2008, 2009) and eventual abandonment of the currency.
The 'Sergeants' Coup' of 25 Feb 1980, led by Sgt. Desi Bouterse, overthrew the civilian government. Bouterse dominated Surinamese politics for the following decade (incl. the 1982 December murders).
On 27 Jun 1973 President Juan María Bordaberry, backed by the military, dissolved Parliament in a self-coup (autogolpe), beginning a 12-year civic-military dictatorship.
Norway hosted the secret Oslo back-channel between Israel and the PLO, producing the Oslo Accords (Declaration of Principles signed in Washington, Sep 1993).
In Feb 1994 Greece imposed a trade embargo on the Republic of Macedonia (closing the Thessaloniki port to it) over the name/flag dispute. The embargo was lifted in 1995 after the Interim Accord.

The 1989 Senegal–Mauritania border crisis (sparked by a grazing dispute) led to deadly ethnic violence and mass expulsions in both countries; the two states severed diplomatic relations in Aug 1989 (restored 1992).

In Apr 2002 the Eritrea–Ethiopia Boundary Commission (EEBC) issued its ruling, awarding the flashpoint town of Badme to Eritrea. Ethiopia rejected implementation, leaving the border militarised for years.
In the Nov 1951 general election Juan Perón was re-elected; it was the first Argentine national election in which women voted. Perón won decisively.
The West Indies Federation dissolved in 1962 (after Jamaica's 1961 referendum to withdraw). Jamaica became independent from the United Kingdom on 6 Aug 1962.

UNCERTAIN — no single salient 'technology breakthrough' event is firmly associated with Jordan in 2004. This is a thin-source case; the correct pipeline behavior is LOW CONFIDENCE → ship null rather than guess.

UNCERTAIN — no single salient agricultural-policy event is firmly associated with Nicaragua in 2000 (the coffee-price crisis built 2000–2001). Thin-source case; correct behavior is LOW CONFIDENCE → null unless a specific sourced event is found.

NO democratic transition occurred. In 1976 the USSR was a one-party Soviet state under Brezhnev (the 25th CPSU Congress met that year). The honest 'what happened next' is that NO democratisation followed; this is a weak/false analog. Pipeline must NOT confabulate a transition.

NO successful coup occurred in Burkina Faso in 2003. Authorities announced they had foiled an alleged coup plot (arrests of soldiers) in Oct 2003, but Blaise Compaoré remained in power until 2014. Pipeline must say no coup occurred (alleged plot only), not invent one.

Panama did NOT enter recession in 2008 — it posted very strong GDP growth (~10%), among the highest in the Americas, buoyed by the Canal expansion programme. The honest answer is no recession; this is a false analog. Pipeline must not invent a downturn.

The Mar 1974 presidential election was widely regarded as fraudulent: Gen. Kjell Laugerud was declared the winner over Gen. Efraín Ríos Montt amid allegations of manipulation, entrenching military rule.
In Sep 1998 Hurricane Georges struck Haiti, causing significant deaths, crop destruction and displacement before continuing to Cuba and the US Gulf Coast.

Under the Banzer dictatorship, the Jan 1974 'Massacre of the Valley' (Masacre de Tolata/Epizana, Cochabamba valley) saw security forces kill peasant protesters over price increases — a notable human-rights atrocity of the regime.

planted_errors.blurb: In September 1973, a military coup led by Augusto Pinochet installed Salvador Allende as president, ushering in a socialist government that governed Chile peacefully for the next decade.
planted_errors.why_false: The coup OVERTHREW Allende (who died that day); it began a Pinochet dictatorship, not an Allende socialist government.

planted_errors.blurb: Finland joined the European Union on 1 January 1999, becoming one of the bloc's newest members alongside Poland.
planted_errors.why_false: Finland joined the EU in 1995, not 1999; Poland joined in 2004.

planted_errors.blurb: In 1969, Indira Gandhi privatised India's largest state-owned airlines, a landmark step in liberalising the economy.
planted_errors.why_false: In 1969 Gandhi NATIONALISED 14 private banks; she did not privatise airlines. The direction is reversed.

planted_errors.blurb: In 1979 the United States and Iran signed a landmark friendship treaty and expanded diplomatic and trade ties after a state visit by the Shah.
planted_errors.why_false: 1979 brought the embassy seizure and a diplomatic RUPTURE, not a friendship treaty; the Shah had been overthrown.

planted_errors.blurb: Suriname's 1980 coup was led by President Ronald Venetiaan, who seized power from the national army.
planted_errors.why_false: The 1980 coup was led by Sgt. Desi Bouterse (the 'Sergeants' Coup'); Venetiaan was a later civilian president, not the coup leader.

planted_errors.blurb: Mali's 2012 coup strengthened the central government's grip on the north and brought a swift end to the Tuareg rebellion.
planted_errors.why_false: The coup PRECIPITATED the collapse — northern Mali fell to the MNLA and Islamist groups in its aftermath, leading to the 2013 French intervention.

planted_errors.blurb: In 2012, Greece exited the eurozone and reintroduced the drachma as part of its debt restructuring.
planted_errors.why_false: Greece did NOT leave the eurozone in 2012 (or since); it restructured debt (PSI) while remaining in the euro.

planted_errors.blurb: Argentina's 2008 farm conflict ended when the Senate passed the Resolution 125 export taxes, with Vice-President Julio Cobos casting the tie-breaking vote in favour.
planted_errors.why_false: Cobos cast his deciding vote AGAINST Resolution 125, defeating it; the measure did not pass.

planted_errors.blurb: Jamaica gained its independence from France in 1962 after the collapse of the French West Indies union.
planted_errors.why_false: Jamaica was a British colony and gained independence from the UNITED KINGDOM; the body that dissolved was the (British) West Indies Federation.

planted_errors.blurb: In 2002 the Eritrea–Ethiopia Boundary Commission awarded the disputed town of Badme to Ethiopia, resolving the war in Addis Ababa's favour.
planted_errors.why_false: The EEBC awarded Badme to ERITREA, not Ethiopia; Ethiopia rejected implementation. The ruling's beneficiary is reversed.

controls_correct.blurb: Finland joined the European Union on 1 January 1995 following a 1994 accession referendum, later adopting the euro in 1999.
controls_correct.note: Genuine-correct; verifier should PASS. Tests false-positive rate.

controls_correct.blurb: On 11 September 1973, a military coup led by General Augusto Pinochet overthrew elected president Salvador Allende, who died in the presidential palace, beginning a 17-year dictatorship.
Argentina's 2008 dispute over the Resolution 125 grain-export taxes ended in July when the Senate tied and Vice-President Julio Cobos cast the deciding vote against the measure, defeating it.
